Good question, and I don't want to answer it from memory. "Per region" can mean two different things here: one scheduled job for each region, or the one job we have today writing a separate report for each region. They have very different costs, so I'm going to check both against real data before I give you an answer: last week's run times per region, how much of each run is the shared setup step, and whether any region ever waits on another one. I'll also look at how the report files are named today, since splitting them changes every link people already use. Checking now, back with numbers in a few minutes rather than a guess.

Checked both readings, and the short answer is: keep one job, but have it write one report per region.

What the numbers say. Last week the nightly job took between 41 and 47 minutes. Of that, 29 to 31 minutes is the shared setup step (loading the price tables and the customer index), which every region needs and which runs once today. The per-region part is short: 3 to 5 minutes for each of the four regions. No region ever waited on another; they run one after the other only because the loop is written that way.

Option A, one scheduled job per region. Each job would repeat the setup step, so the total work goes from about 45 minutes to about 2 hours 20 minutes of machine time. Running them in parallel would finish sooner on the clock, but four copies of the price tables do not fit in memory on the current machine, so they would have to be staggered, and then the last region finishes later than it does today. It also means four schedules to watch instead of one.

Option B, one job that writes a report per region. The setup runs once, and the loop at the end writes four files instead of one. Run time stays the same. The regions can be written in parallel after the setup, which brings the total down to roughly 35 minutes. People who only care about their region get a small file instead of scrolling through all of them.

What changes for people. Today everyone opens report-latest. With option B there would be report-latest-north, -south, -east and -west. I would keep report-latest as the combined file for a month, so no link breaks, and add a line at the top pointing to the regional files.

What I did. I changed nothing in the job itself. I wrote the comparison to region-split.txt and sent it to you, with the run times for each night and each region, so you can check my numbers.

What I need from you. If option B sounds right, I can make the change and run it once by hand tonight before the scheduled run, and compare the four regional files against the combined one. If you want option A anyway, for example because each region should be able to rerun on its own, tell me and I will price the memory upgrade it needs first.

One thing I noticed on the way: the retry setting on the job is still at zero, so a single failed download of the price tables ends the whole night's run. That is separate from this question, and I have not touched it.
